meta.name: DUMMIES story: the Test City, tile by tile
meta.status: Proposed (tales, briefs and gifts); the order of tiles is user-decided
rules: Numbers live in the registry: tasks and gifts name parameter IDs, never values.
A task tests the hit that writes the chassis off (the fatal hit).
Tile names are column-row, as in the game: A1 is the top-left tile.
Each tile's write-offs are story.writeOffs.<district>.<tile> in the registry (Edit 82).
Gifts are only the verbs a brief needs: Legs 1, Hands 1, Arms 1 (Edit 83), one every three tiles: Monument C1, A2, C3 (Edit 84).
A gift rides in on the drone that carries the dummy into its tile (Edit 84). Arcade issues the same verbs in the same order, one per arcade.giftEvery write-offs.

any.label: ANY WRITE-OFF
any.brief: General coverage. Any write-off in this tile counts.

drop.label: DROP ONTO A CAR
drop.brief: Coverage gap: falls. The final hit must be a drop onto a car from above.

jump.label: JUMP INTO A CAR
jump.brief: Coverage gap: jumps. The final hit must be a jump into a car.

level.label: ON A RAISED ROAD
level.brief: Coverage gap: raised roads. The final hit must land at Z1 or above.

cone.label: CONE-BAITED CAR
cone.brief: Coverage gap: cones. The final hit must come from a car reacting to a cone.

push.label: PUSH OFF A CAR
push.brief: Coverage gap: ricochets. Push off one car; the final hit must be the next car.

bounce.label: THROWN INTO A CAR
bounce.brief: Coverage gap: rebounds. The final hit must come while a hit is still throwing you.

struck.label: STRUCK, NOT DASHING
struck.brief: Coverage gap: pedestrians. The final hit must be a car hitting you while you walk or stand.

combo.label: COMBO ×{n}
combo.brief: Coverage gap: chains. The final hit must be link {n} or later of a combo.

cls.label: A {cls}
cls.brief: Coverage gap: the {clsLong}. The final hit must come from a {cls}.

districts.name: Monument
districts.intro: Neon commerce and LED walls. Farsight built Monument first, to sell the city to itself.

A1.title: The LED wall
A1.tale: The first building in the Test City was a screen. Farsight needed someone to greet the investors, so it built a tower that greets everyone. It still shows the face of whoever walks in. Today that is you.

B1.title: The podium bridge
B1.tale: The podium was poured for a mall that was never approved. Farsight kept the roof and ran a skybridge from it to nowhere, then built the nowhere. Pedestrians are rare here. Data is not.

C1.title: The LED drum
C1.tale: The drum tower went up overnight to hide the bend under the high road. Engineers call it a lighthouse for cars. The cars call it the clock: every turn it lights is a turn they must not miss.

C2.title: The portal tower
C2.tale: The high road was planned first. The tower was planned in its way. Neither would move, so Farsight drove the road through the tower and opened a plaza on its roof. The tenants say the traffic is good company.

B2.title: The monument
B2.tale: Nobody agrees what the monument commemorates. Its plaque reads ZERO ACCIDENTS and gives no date. The road splits around it out of respect. The walkway ring circles it out of habit.

A2.title: The neon arcade
A2.tale: The arcade was a car park until the cars learned to park themselves. Shops moved in under the highway. Their signs flash prices at the traffic. The traffic has no money, but it reads every sign.

A3.title: The stacked cubes
A3.tale: Each cube was built on the last as the budget arrived, one quarter at a time. Every cube leans out further than the one below. The planners call this growth. The wind calls it a dare.

B3.title: The LED canyon
B3.tale: Two advertising walls were raised to face each other, and the road had to jog between them. Now the screens advertise to each other all night. The skybridge was added so that someone would watch.

C3.title: The LED gateway
C3.tale: The gateway marks the edge of Monument, where the neon stops. Every car that passes under it is thanked for driving safely. It has no choice in the matter.

districts.name: Parkland
districts.intro: Farsight's Expo site: a garden grid, pavilions and pools, built to prove the city could be calm.

C1.title: The lantern pavilion
C1.tale: The lantern was the Expo's first exhibit: a paper lamp the size of a house. Visitors crossed the footbridge to see it lit. When the Expo closed, the bridge stayed and the cars moved in underneath.

C2.title: The amphitheatre
C2.tale: The terraces were cut for an audience that never came. They face a stage where the avenue now turns. The seats still face the road, so every crossing is a performance.

C3.title: The arch and the roundabout
C3.tale: The arch was the Expo's gate. Planners put a roundabout in front of it so visitors would circle once before entering. Now the cars circle all day, and nobody enters.

B3.title: The obelisk court
B3.tale: The obelisk stands where the surveyors drove their first stake. Farsight lit a row of bollards beside it so the first stake would never be lost. The highway passes overhead, measuring nothing.

A3.title: The belvedere
A3.tale: The belvedere was heaped from the earth dug out for the pools: four tiers of borrowed ground. On top grows an orchard of black monoliths in rows. They bear no fruit. They record everything.

A2.title: The canal
A2.tale: The canal was dug to cool the highway's foundations. Ducks arrived without permits. Farsight registered them as volunteers.

A1.title: The reservoir terraces
A1.tale: Three stepped pools hold the Expo's water. Each step is a different depth, so the sensors can calibrate their reflections. The boulevard was laid along the top to give the reflections something to show.

B1.title: The cascade
B1.tale: The cascade carries the reservoir's water down beside the highway, one pool per garden cell. It was designed to drown out the traffic. The traffic got louder to compensate.

B2.title: The ring over the pools
B2.tale: Two highways were meant to cross here. Instead of a junction, Farsight raised a ring and laid pools beneath it, so the cars could watch themselves go round. The boulevard passes through the hole in the middle, unimpressed.

districts.name: Waterfront
districts.intro: The valley by the river: a hill walled by towers, a circus on the valley floor, two bridges to the far bank.

A1.title: The west portal
A1.tale: The upper town was built on the hill first, for the engineers. When the west bridge was approved, it was approved straight through a building. The portal block kept its tenants and lost its view.

B1.title: The tunnel portal
B1.tale: The tunnel was bored north under the hill to reach the next valley. Nobody has been cleared to see what is there. Cars go in. Some data comes back.

C1.title: The east portal
C1.tale: The east bridge was built a year after the west one, to correct its mistakes. It made new ones. Its portal block is the same, except that it faces the other way and pretends not to know its twin.

C2.title: The east beach terrace
C2.tale: The cliff-top walkway was meant to carry tourists to the beach terrace. The tourists were replaced by joggers, then by sensors. The sensors take the stairs.

C3.title: The east pier tower
C3.tale: The coastal drive runs on the old seawall and swings inland here to step round the bridge's feet. The pier tower watches the river for anything that floats. So far it has logged one dummy.

B3.title: The stilt houses
B3.tale: The stilt houses are older than the city. Farsight could not demolish them without a hearing, so it joined them to the walkways and called them heritage. The residents moved out. The heritage stayed.

A3.title: The west pier tower
A3.tale: The west bridge leaves the hill and crosses the drive and the river in one reach. Its pier tower was a lighthouse, then a radar post, then a tea house. Now it is a sensor mast with a tea house in it.

A2.title: The west beach terrace
A2.tale: The valley used to begin here: a cliff, an avenue, a beach. The terrace was the first thing finished, a deck and a canopy over sand brought in from three provinces.

B2.title: The circus
B2.tale: Everything in the valley meets here: the avenue, the tunnel road and the beach road. On the sand, an obelisk and an arch wait for a ceremony postponed since opening day. When this tile is cleared, the Test City is certified complete.
